answer: Rewards are tallied per network prefix, not per key. Each prefix the registry sees gets a public label from a fixed list -- willow, velvet, juniper -- and every account resolving there draws on one shared payout weight, split by a square-root rule. A thousand keys behind a single rented link settle like roughly thirty identities; an operator with three unrelated providers keeps three full weights. Faking a crowd then costs bandwidth contracts, abuse histories and dead leases, none of which scale with key generation, the cheap step. Honest agents lose nothing; farms must buy distinct routes.
